title: Daily Practice: Ch 1 Chemical Reactions and Equations
subject: Science
chapter: Chemical Reactions and Equations · Week 1 of the 90-day plan
instructions: One day at a time, about 25 minutes each. Do Day 1 on the day you study the chapter, then Day 2 and Day 3 on the next two days.
Write your answers in your notebook, then check them with the key the same day. Copy every mistake into your error log.
Every equation you write must be balanced. Count every atom on both sides!

questions.q: Magnesium ribbon burns with a dazzling white flame and turns into a white powder. The white powder is:
We balance a chemical equation so that it obeys the law of:
questions.answer: (c) conservation of mass: atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a reaction

questions.q: Which state symbol shows that a substance is dissolved in water?
Heating limestone (CaCO_{3}) to make quicklime is an example of:
questions.answer: (b) a thermal decomposition reaction: CaCO_{3}(s) → CaO(s) + CO_{2}(g)

questions.q: What does the arrow (→) in a chemical equation mean? On which side do we write the reactants?
questions.answer: The arrow means 'gives' or 'forms', and shows the direction of the reaction. Reactants are written on the left, products on the right.

questions.q: Write a balanced equation with state symbols: solid zinc reacts with aqueous copper sulphate to give aqueous zinc sulphate and solid copper.
Hydrogen gas combines with chlorine gas to form hydrogen chloride gas. Write the balanced equation and name the type of reaction.
questions.answer: H_{2}(g) + Cl_{2}(g) → 2HCl(g). It is a combination reaction (two substances form one product).

questions.q: Which of the following is a double displacement reaction?
questions.answer: (d) Na_{2}SO_{4} + BaCl_{2} → BaSO_{4} + 2NaCl: the two compounds exchange ions

questions.q: An iron nail is kept in copper sulphate solution for about 20 minutes. The nail:
questions.answer: (a) gets a brownish coating of copper, because iron displaces copper

questions.q: In the reaction MnO_{2} + 4HCl → MnCl_{2} + 2H_{2}O + Cl_{2}, the substance that is reduced is:
questions.answer: (a) MnO_{2}: it loses oxygen. (HCl is oxidised: it loses hydrogen.)

questions.q: Why is respiration called an exothermic reaction? Write the balanced equation for the breakdown of glucose in our cells.
questions.answer:
Respiration releases energy, so it is exothermic.
C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}(aq) + 6O_{2}(aq) → 6CO_{2}(aq) + 6H_{2}O(l) + energy

questions.q: Silver bromide is used in black-and-white photography. Write the balanced equation for what happens when it is exposed to light, and name the type of reaction.
questions.answer: 2AgBr(s) → 2Ag(s) + Br_{2}(g) in light. Photolytic decomposition (decomposition by light). The silver formed makes the image dark.

questions.q:
Name the type of each reaction and give a reason:
(i) NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H_{2}O
(ii) 2FeSO_{4} → Fe_{2}O_{3} + SO_{2} + SO_{3} (on heating)
(iii) Mg + 2HCl → MgCl_{2} + H_{2}
questions.answer:
(i) Double displacement (neutralisation): the two compounds exchange ions.
(ii) Thermal decomposition: one substance breaks into simpler ones on heating.
(iii) Displacement: the more reactive metal, magnesium, displaces hydrogen from the acid.

questions.q: Zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, but copper does not. Write the balanced equation for the reaction that happens, and explain what this tells you about the reactivity of zinc and copper compared with hydrogen.
questions.answer: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl_{2} + H_{2}. Zinc is more reactive than hydrogen, so it displaces hydrogen from the acid. Copper is less reactive than hydrogen, so it cannot displace it and there is no reaction.

questions.q:
**Assertion (A):** Most decomposition reactions are endothermic.
**Reason (R):** Energy, as heat, light or electricity, is needed to break a compound into simpler substances.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.answer: (a) Both are true, and R explains A.

questions.q:
Which of these changes involve oxidation?
(i) rusting of iron  (ii) rancidity of butter  (iii) respiration  (iv) melting of wax
questions.answer: (b) (i), (ii) and (iii). Melting of wax is a physical change.

questions.q: A student dipped a clean copper wire into colourless silver nitrate solution. After an hour, the solution had turned blue, and a shiny greyish-white deposit had formed on the wire.

subparts.q: Name the deposit on the wire. Why did the solution turn blue?
subparts.answer: The deposit is silver. The solution turned blue because copper nitrate formed, and copper salts in solution are blue.

subparts.q: Write the balanced equation with state symbols.
Name the type of reaction. What does it tell you about copper and silver?
subparts.answer: A displacement reaction. Copper is more reactive than silver, so it displaces silver from its salt solution.

questions.q:
(a) Burning magnesium keeps burning in carbon dioxide: 2Mg + CO_{2} → 2MgO + C. Which substance is oxidised and which is reduced?
(b) Why is hydrogen peroxide stored in dark-coloured bottles? Write the balanced equation.
(c) Write the balanced equation for the burning of methane (natural gas) and say whether it is exothermic or endothermic.
questions.answer:
(a) Mg is oxidised (gains oxygen to form MgO). CO_{2} is reduced (loses oxygen to form carbon).
(b) Light decomposes it: 2H_{2}O_{2} → 2H_{2}O + O_{2}. Dark bottles keep light out.
(c) CH_{4} + 2O_{2} → CO_{2} + 2H_{2}O + heat. Exothermic (combustion gives out heat).

questions.q:
A student adds barium chloride solution to sodium sulphate solution in a test tube.
(i) What does she see?
(ii) Write the balanced equation with state symbols.
(iii) Name the type of reaction, and give one more example of the same type.
questions.answer:
(i) A white precipitate forms.
(ii) Na_{2}SO_{4}(aq) + BaCl_{2}(aq) → BaSO_{4}(s) + 2NaCl(aq)
(iii) Double displacement (precipitation) reaction. Another example: AgNO_{3}(aq) + NaCl(aq) → AgCl(s) + NaNO_{3}(aq), a white precipitate of silver chloride.

closing: Three days, one chapter done. Now put your mistakes in the error log!
